chunks: From him, from Ibn Muskān, from al-Ḥalabī, from Abū ‘Abdillāh (peace be upon him), like it.

key_terms.أَبُو عَبْدِ اللَّهِ: Abū ‘Abdillāh (Imam al-Sādiq), the source of the narration
key_terms.ابْنُ مُسْكَانَ: Ibn Muskān, a narrator in the chain
key_terms.الْحَلَبِيُّ: Al-Ḥalabī, a narrator in the chain
key_terms.مِثْلَهُ: Like it / similar to it, indicating the content repeats the previous hadith

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on a woman divorced three times according to this hadith?
ai.summary: This concise narration from Shaykh al-Tusi’s *al-Istibsar* confirms the consensus that a woman divorced three times in a single sitting (or sequence) does not become lawful to her first husband until she marries another man and that marriage is consummated and subsequently dissolved. It reinforces the Shia jurisprudential view that the 'waiting period' for triple divorce is contingent upon a valid intermediate marriage (*Nikah al-Mahill*), distinguishing it from the Sunni view of *Talaq al-Sunnah* in many contexts. The repetition highlights the certainty of this ruling within the chapter's thematic focus on the mechanics of remarriage after triple divorce.
